name: Nicotinamide riboside and NAD+ precursors
short: Placebo-controlled trials of up to 8 weeks found adverse events no more common than with placebo; a meta-analysis of NMN trials agreed. Long-term safety is not established.
text: In an 8-week randomised placebo-controlled trial in overweight adults, nicotinamide riboside at 100, 300 or 1000 mg/day caused no flushing and no significant difference in adverse events compared with placebo. A small 4-week phase I trial in Parkinson's disease using 1500 mg twice daily found no moderate or severe adverse events, although recipients showed a slight initial rise in serum homocysteine. A meta-analysis of randomised trials of nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), another NAD+ precursor, lasting 14 days to 24 weeks found no increase in overall, serious or withdrawal-related adverse events or in liver enzymes; its authors called for longer trials to confirm long-term safety. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
